Hardware Engineering Intern
This role has been designed as ‘’Onsite’ with an expectation that you will primarily work from an HPE office.

Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.
Job Description:
Responsibilities:
Support senior team members on assigned technical projects as determined by the business unit.
Help identify and troubleshoot technical issues.
Actively provide hands-on support in the lab for hardware quality initiatives and suggest solutions.
Interface with cross-functional teams during the product development cycle.
Engage in learning about new technologies and methodologies relevant to work.
Fulfill tasks and responsibilities assigned by a supervisor in a timely and efficient manner.
Participate in periodic reviews to share updates and incorporate feedback on assigned projects/initiatives.
Education & Experience:
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.
Solid experience and proficiency with electrical circuit design, schematic design and schematic capture tools. Clear proficiency with multiple aspects of hardware design, which may include digital logic design, CPU subsystem design, clocks, signal integrity, power delivery and analog components.
Experience with board design layout and familiarity with multiple-layer board considerations.
Team project experience outside of coursework.
Hands-on experience testing L2/L3 products with Ethernet packet generators.
Knowledge & Skills:
Passion for building hardware projects and solving challenging problems.
Skilled debugging capability and intrinsically curious about how things work.
Understanding of how PCIe, Ethernet, I2C and high speed SerDes work at the hardware level.
Capable scripting skills using Python.
Good communication and interpersonal skills.
Self-motivated team player, and capable of working in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Understanding of Ethernet routing and switching.
Familiarity with FPGAs and Verilog.
Comfortable in a Unix/Linux environment.
Impact/Scope:
University students actively enrolled in a university/college/institution pursuing a Bachelor's degree in a technical area of study, and who typically works during school breaks and then returns to their university. While this applies to most interns, there may be opportunities for full-time students to work as part-time interns during the school year in some countries.
